content_metadata.description: This video tutorial demonstrates how to export presentations from PowerPoint and Google Slides using different methods and formats.

qAndA.answer: It can be saved in either MP4 or Quicktime format.
qAndA.question: Where can the exported PowerPoint file be saved?
Where can you find the Google Slides Add-on 'Creator Studio'?

qAndA.answer: It requests permissions to access your Google account and Google Drive.
qAndA.question: What permissions does 'Creator Studio' ask for?

qAndA.answer: It has four export formats: animated gif, image sequence, video file and video file with audio.
qAndA.question: How many different export formats does 'Creator Studio' have?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Microsoft Powerpoint has a very useful feature that is still missing inside Google slides
and that is you can easily export your PowerPoint presentations into a video file.
So here I am inside PowerPoint and if I go to the file menu and then choose Export, I
can save this presentation as an MP4 video or a quick time movie.
Now this is a very handy feature because I can now share this presentation on a video
site like YouTube or even uploaded to Facebook.
Now if you are a Google slides user and would still like to export your presentations to
video formats, check out Creator Studio.
Now this is a Google slides add-on that lets you export your presentations as animated
Jeff Images and video files.
You get started go to Creator Studio or Dev and install the add-on.
The first time you use this add-on it will request certain permissions because it has
to access your presentations to convert them into different formats and it also requires
permissions to Google Drive because it will automatically upload the converted files to
your Google Drive.
So just click allow and your add-on is installed.
So here I am inside Google slides, I will go to the add-on's menu and then choose Creator
Studio from the drop-down.
So first you need to specify the width of the exported file in pixels.
Now you just need to specify the width here and Creator Studio will automatically calculate
the height of the exported file to maintain the original aspect ratio of the presentation.
Next you need to specify the time interval between slides and this is in seconds.
So for instance if you are making a Jeff image and you would like each slide to stay on
the screen for 4 seconds you can just put 4 here.
I will put 2.5 to speed things up.
So the image is now ready and it is automatically added to my Google Drive.
I can click this eye icon to view the exported file.
And I can also hit this download button to save the exported file from Google Drive to
my local computer.
Okay, let's now try the next export format and that is an image sequence.
So basically Creator Studio will take screenshots of each slide in your presentation and save
them as a number sequence in your Google Drive.
So for this export format I will slightly increase the output resolution to say 1,280 pixels.
So the files have been saved and I can click this eye icon again to open the corresponding
folder in Google Drive.
And there you have all the slide images sequentially numbered.
Next let's try the video format.
So let's say I want to keep a 2 second gap between each slide and I will not touch the
output width because this is good for HD video.
Hit the go button and your video would be ready in few seconds.
The time may vary depending on the number of slides in your presentation.
So the video is ready.
I hit the download button to save the file to my computer and let's preview it.
And this looks good.
Okay, let's now try the last export format which is the most interesting one because in
addition to video you can also add background audio to your video.
Now this audio may be background music or if you have voice narration that you have recorded
elsewhere you can just upload it here and it will play alongside the presentation.
So I'll select the video with audio option and then you have an option to upload an audio
file.
Now you can upload audio files in all the popular audio formats preferably MP3 or WAVE.
So the audio file has been uploaded now.
Now in case you want to replace this with another audio file just hit that cancel button
to upload another file.
For this example we will not do that and I'll hit go button to render the video.
So that was a quick demo of creator studio for Google slides.
Go to createestudio.dev and install it now.
Thanks.

youtube_description:
Convert Google Slides presentations to movies and animated GIF images with Creator Studio. You can also add background music and voice narration to your presentation videos. 

Download from https://creatorstudio.dev
